newsitem.title: UK: S&P rates Siebe corp credit A plus l-term.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Siebe corp credit A plus l-term.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Monday it assigned its A-plus long-term and A1 short-term corporate credit ratings to Siebe Plc.
The outlook on the long-term rating is stable, S&P said in a statement.
"The ratings reflect U.K.-based Siebe's position as a leading diversified engineering group, and a strong financial profile," S&P said.

Siebe's main product areas are temperature, appliance, and power controls, process automation and control systems, and specialist industrial equipment. These are mostly knowledge-intensive sectors, where competitive advantage is sustained by technological leadership, software and service quality, and low cost production, S&P said.
Group sales, which totaled 2.6 billion stg (about US$4.0 billion) in the year to April 6, 1996, are well diversified both geographically and by end-user industry, S&P said.
This, and the fact that the group is exposed to all stages of the economic cycle, helps to mitigate the cyclicality normally associated with the engineering sector, S&P said.

"Growth opportunities stem from Siebe's strong presence in developing economies, and from the gradual shift towards electronic and software- based products, which favors the group. Organic growth has been supplemented by a series of sizable acquisitions over the last 10 years to strengthen the group's position in its core markets," S&P said.
Most of these acquisitions have been financed with equity, allowing Siebe to maintain a conservative financial profile, S&P said.
The largest and most recent acquisition, of Unitech Plc (for 590 million stg in May 1996), gives Siebe a leading position in the fast-growing electronic power controls market.

Operating profit margins after depreciation have been consistently strong and stable, averaging 14.3 percent in the five years to April 1996, S&P said. Cash flow is also strong; funds from operations to net debt has averaged 87 percent in the last 3 years, and discretionary cash flow is also robust. Net debt to capital, after adjusting for goodwill written off, stood at a moderate 22.5 percent at April 6, 1996, though the figure including capitalised operating leases would be higher, at about 32 percent.
"Though the acquisition of Unitech was a sizable one, its operations make a good strategic fit with the group, and it was conservatively financed," S&P said.
"Siebe is expected to maintain its strong financial profile whilst continuing to enjoy above average growth rates," S&P said.
